settings.description:
A garden of more than 400 camellia cultivars.
Photographed, remembered, and grown with care.

albums.name: Saika
albums.description: Latest Illustrated Book of Japanese Camellias, (Camellias of Japan), 2010, p.56 with colour photo; Medium size single, pink ground shading to white at the centre, tubular shape, central column of stamens with white filaments. Flowers mid-season to late. Leaves elliptic, flat. Upright growth. A natural seedling of Seiōbo, grown in 1995 by Takashi Shiota, Ishikawa Pref., Japan, named and released in 2007.

albums.name: Huanle Juhui (Joyous Party)
albums.description: Gao Jiyin et al. 2016. Illustrations of the New Camellias Hybrids that Bloom Year-round. P.100. [C. japonica ‘Tama Beauty’ ×C. azalea](Joyous Party). Flowers peach-red in summer and red with slight-purple tone in cold seasons, hazy white patches on the petal-surfaces, central small petals with small white patches, anemone form, medium to large. Leaves dark-green, margins nearly smooth. Plant upright and growth vigorous. Blooms fully in summer, autumn and winter, but sparsely in spring.

albums.name: Sanpei-tsubaki
albums.description: Color: Pink with white margins with yellow anthers and light pink filaments. Form: Single; 6-7 petals. Size: Medium. Bloom Season: E. Growth Rate: Average. Growth Characteristics: Upright growth. Leaf Characteristics: Medium green. Place of Origination: Japan. Year of Registration / Origination: 1966. Other Information: Named for Oguri, Sanpei in the 1950's by Adachi, Choka.

albums.name: Shuchuka
albums.description: White with narrow picotee edge of Red. Miniature to small, semidouble to peony form. L. (Japan 1879 - Chin-Ka-Shu).

albums.name: Kamo-Hon-Ami
albums.description: ('Hon-Ami', 'Sotan'). White. Large, single. E-M. (Similar to 'Amabilis'). (Japan 1935 - Chugai).

albums.name: Rokukasen
albums.description: JCS., Japan Camellia, 1986, No.22, p.4, colour photo: Originated in a garden in Hamakita City, selected by Muramatsu and named by Hakoda. Single, small to medium size. A spring flowering sasanqua, white variegation on peach-red background. Petals at intervals having a dappled pattern and size variation. Hakoda, JCS, 1987, Tsubaki, No.26, p.51 as 'Rokkasen': Red ground with white spots. Blooms early to mid-season. Different reading 'Rokkasen'. Discovered by Tsoyushi Matsumura in Hamamatsu City, Shizuoka Prefecture, Japan, late 1970s, named by Naotoshi Hakoda. International Camellia Society, 2023. Splendid Sasanquas, an International Ornament, p.71.

albums.name: Scented Gem
albums.description: Fuchsia Pink with White petaloids. Miniature, anemone form. Open, upright growth. E-M. Fragrant. (Lutchuensis x Japonica 'Tinsie'). (U.S. 1983 - Domoto).

albums.name: Sugar Dream
albums.description: Pink. Medium, anemone form. Average, open, upright growth, E. (Reticulata hybrid 'Dream Girl' x Oleifera 'Jaune'). (N.Z. 1984 - O. Blumhardt, Whangarei).

albums.name: Frank Gibson
albums.description: White with mass of White petaloids edged Yellow. Medium, anemone form. Vigorous, open, upright growth. E-M. (U.S. 1951 - Mrs. F. L. Gibson, Thomasville, GA).

albums.name: Panaché de Gaujacq
albums.description: Single flower with 8–10 deep pink petals with white mottling and stripes; seedling of C. hiemalis with possible C. sasanqua “Variegata” pollen (first flowering 1996).

albums.name: Tinker Bell
albums.description: White striped Pink and Rose Red. Small, anemone form. Vigorous, upright growth. E-M. (For another form of this cultivar see 'Jingle Bells'). (U.S. 1958 - Nuccio's).

albums.name: Fubuki-shiratama
albums.description: Seibundō Shinkōsha, "Garden Life", 1975, Tsubaki to Sazanka, with colour photo inside back cover: A campanulate to cup-shaped single of 5-6 petals, blush pink, speckled crimson, central stamen cluster with golden yellow anthers. Early to mid-season flowering. Leaves oval, medium size, acuminate, thick, smooth, shallowly, sharply serrate. Slightly fragrant. See colour photo No.362, p.148, Encyclopedia of Camellias in Colour, vol.II, 1978, and p.133, Seibundō Shinkōsha, 1979, Senchinshū, description p.244. Nippon Tsubaki - Sasanqua Meikan, 1998, p.226 with colour photo; English translation p.158. A natural seedling of Shiratama. Originated in Kawaguchi City, named and released by Eiichi Kaneko, Tokorozawa City around 1960.

albums.name: Tama-Ariake
albums.description: from Nagasaki Pref. Japan Camellia No.78, August 2005; A crossing of Tama-no-ura × Iwane-shibori. Red bordered white, semi-double to peony form, split stamens, medium to large. Blooming early to mid-season. Leaves lanceolate, medium. Branches weeping. Tree vigorous. Originated by Kaoru Kusumoto.

albums.name: Camellia perpetua
albums.description: Camellia perpetua S. Y. Liang et L. D. Huang, sect. Chrysantha (golden camellias); ICR lists this name as a synonym of Camellia chuongtsoensis. Nanning Golden Camellia Park, 2021, Golden Camellia Species of China and Abroad (国内外金花茶物种图鉴), pp.80-81: Evergreen shrub, 2-5 m tall. Young leaves purplish brown; mature leaves thinly leathery, elliptic, 6.5-8.0 cm long, dark grey-green and glossy above, finely serrate. Flowers golden yellow, mostly solitary, terminal or axillary, 5.7-8.0 cm across; petals 12-14, oval to ovate, apex rounded or slightly notched; stamens in 4-5 whorls, filaments 1.6-2.2 cm; styles 3-5, free. Capsule flattened-globose, 2.6-3.9 cm across. Flowers in several seasons each year, peaking May to July. Endemic to Chongzuo, Guangxi, China, in limestone evergreen forest at about 350 m.

albums.name: Sweetie Pie
albums.description: Blush Pink with one or more Red stripes. Large to very large, semidouble with occasional rabbit ears. Vigorous, upright growth. E-M. (U.S. 1997 - D. Fitzgerald, Orlando, FL).

albums.name: Secchū-no-ka
albums.description: Chu Kuo-Tung & Tsai Tsan-Yu, 2011, Taiwan Camellia Genealogy (台灣茶花族譜), p.237. (C. hybrid). Originated in Japan, 2008. Hiemalis 'Kanjiro' x C. yuhsienensis. Flowers white with pale pink at the base, or with pale pink inner petals. Semidouble with wavy petals and spreading, plum-blossom type stamens. Large (10 cm). Blooms December to January. Fragrant.
